1	// What the panel shows of a trail, from `entire trail show --json` and `entire trail finding list --json`
2	// (shapes in test/fixtures/trail-*.json): the change this branch is, its merge gates and review, and
3	// its open findings. Entire's text is untrusted; the panel renders it as text only.
4	const BODY_LIMIT = 400
5	const FINDING_LIMIT = 20
6	const TEXT_LIMIT = 200
7	const LIST_LIMIT = 30
8	
9	export function trailSummary(trail, { findings = null, diff = null } = {}) {
10	  const changes = Array.isArray(trail.changes) ? trail.changes : []
11	  const current = changes.find((change) => change.current) ?? changes.find((change) => change.mergeability) ?? null
12	  const about = findings?.trail ?? {}
13	  const summary = {
14	    number: trail.number ?? null,
15	    title: trail.title ?? '',
16	    status: trail.status ?? null,
17	    type: trail.type ?? null,
18	    priority: trail.priority && trail.priority !== 'none' ? trail.priority : null,
19	    body: typeof trail.body === 'string' ? trail.body.slice(0, BODY_LIMIT) : '',
20	    repository: current?.repository ?? null,
21	    change: current?.number ?? null,
22	    changeStatus: current?.status ?? null,
23	    branch: current?.branch ?? about.branch ?? null,
24	    base: about.base ?? null,
25	    author: about.author?.login ?? null,
26	    createdAt: trail.createdAt ?? null,
27	    mergedAt: about.mergedAt ?? null,
28	    diff,
29	    changes: changes.map((change) => ({
30	      repository: change.repository ?? '',
31	      branch: change.branch ?? '',
32	      status: change.status ?? null,
33	      current: change === current
34	    })),
35	    merge: current?.mergeability ? mergeSummary(current.mergeability, about.base) : null,
36	    findings: findings ? findingsSummary(findings) : null
37	  }
38	  return { ...summary, open: summary.changeStatus === 'open' && summary.status !== 'closed', blockers: mergeBlockers(summary) }
39	}
40	
41	// Why the panel's Merge button stays off, one short line each; empty when it may merge. Merging needs
42	// the change open, an approval (when the repo has an approvals gate), every blocking gate passed, no
43	// conflicts, and Entire's own word that it merges. Entire checks the gates again when it merges.
44	export function mergeBlockers(summary) {
45	  if (summary.changeStatus !== 'open' || summary.status === 'closed') return [`The change is ${summary.changeStatus ?? 'not open'}`]
46	  const merge = summary.merge
47	  if (!merge) return ['Entire reported no merge gates for this change']
48	  const blockers = []
49	  if (merge.conflicts) blockers.push(`Conflicts with ${summary.base ?? 'the base branch'}`)
50	  const approvals = merge.gates.find((gate) => gate.type === 'approvals')
51	  if (approvals && approvals.status !== 'passed') blockers.push(`Not approved yet (${approvals.summary ?? approvals.status})`)
52	  for (const gate of merge.gates) {
53	    if (gate === approvals || !gate.blocking || gate.status === 'passed') continue
54	    blockers.push(`${gate.key.replace(/_/g, ' ')}: ${gate.summary ?? gate.status}`)
55	  }
56	  if (!blockers.length && !merge.mergeable) blockers.push('Entire says this change can’t merge yet')
57	  return blockers
58	}
59	
60	function mergeSummary(mergeability, base) {
61	  const gates = mergeability.gates ?? []
62	  const findingsGate = gates.find((gate) => gate.gate_type === 'findings')
63	  return {
64	    mergeable: Boolean(mergeability.mergeable),
65	    conflicts: mergeability.conflict_status && !['clean', 'unknown'].includes(mergeability.conflict_status) ? mergeability.conflict_status : null,
66	    gates: gates.map((gate) => ({
67	      key: gate.gate_key ?? gate.gate_type ?? 'gate',
68	      type: gate.gate_type ?? null,
69	      blocking: Boolean(gate.blocking),
70	      status: gate.status ?? 'unknown',
71	      evaluated: gate.state !== 'not_run',
72	      rationale: text(gate.rationale),
73	      summary: gateSummary(gate, base),
74	      people: gate.gate_type === 'approvals' ? approvers(gate) : [],
75	      at: gate.completed_at ?? null,
76	      sha: gate.evaluated_at_sha ? String(gate.evaluated_at_sha).slice(0, 7) : null,
77	      // Evaluated on an earlier commit than the change's head.
78	      outdated: Boolean(gate.evaluated_at_sha && gate.head_sha && gate.evaluated_at_sha !== gate.head_sha),
79	      staleReason: gate.stale_reason ? text(gate.stale_reason) : null,
80	      detail: gateDetail(gate, mergeability)
81	    })),
82	    review: findingsGate ? reviewSummary(findingsGate) : null
83	  }
84	}
85	
86	function text(value) {
87	  return String(value ?? '').slice(0, TEXT_LIMIT)
88	}
89	
90	// What the panel shows when a gate is opened: who approved, each check run, the review behind the
91	// findings gate, or how far behind the base the branch is.
92	function gateDetail(gate, mergeability) {
93	  const value = gate.value ?? {}
94	  const config = value.config ?? {}
95	  if (gate.gate_type === 'approvals') {
96	    return {
97	      approved: value.approved ?? 0,
98	      required: value.required ?? config.min_reviewers ?? 0,
99	      changesRequested: Boolean(value.changes_requested),
100	      staleDismissed: value.stale_dismissed ?? 0,
101	      selfExcluded: Boolean(value.self_excluded),
102	      selfApproval: config.allow_self_approval ?? null,
103	      dismissStale: config.dismiss_stale_approvals_on_push ?? null,
104	      reviewers: gateReviewers(gate)
105	    }
106	  }
107	  if (gate.gate_type === 'checks') {
108	    // The change's own runs carry the app and timing; the gate's copy is the fallback.
109	    const runs = mergeability.checks?.runs?.length ? mergeability.checks.runs : (value.checks ?? [])
110	    return {
111	      requireAll: config.require_all_success ?? null,
112	      required: (config.required_checks ?? []).slice(0, LIST_LIMIT).map((check) => text(check?.name ?? check)),
113	      total: value.total_count ?? runs.length,
114	      runs: runs.slice(0, LIST_LIMIT).map((run) => ({
115	        name: text(run.name ?? 'check'),
116	        app: run.app_name ? text(run.app_name) : null,
117	        status: run.conclusion ?? run.status ?? 'unknown',
118	        startedAt: run.started_at ?? null,
119	        completedAt: run.completed_at ?? null
120	      }))
121	    }
122	  }
123	  if (gate.gate_type === 'findings') {
124	    if (gate.state === 'not_run' || !gate.value) return null
125	    const review = reviewSummary(gate)
126	    return {
127	      minSeverity: config.agent_findings_min_severity ?? null,
128	      blocking: value.agent_blocking_findings ?? gate.finding_count ?? 0,
129	      reviewedHead: value.reviewed_head ?? null,
130	      inFlight: review.inFlight,
131	      reviewers: review.reviewers.slice(0, LIST_LIMIT),
132	      severity: review.severity
133	    }
134	  }
135	  if (gate.gate_type === 'up_to_date') {
136	    if (gate.state === 'not_run' || !gate.value) return null
137	    return {
138	      behindBy: value.behind_by ?? 0,
139	      compare: value.compare_status ?? null,
140	      allowBehind: config.allow_behind_if_mergeable ?? null
141	    }
142	  }
143	  return null
144	}
145	
146	// Everyone who reviewed, once each, with where they landed.
147	function gateReviewers(gate) {
148	  const seen = new Set()
149	  return [gate.reviewers, gate.value?.reviewers]
150	    .flat()
151	    .filter((reviewer) => reviewer?.login && !seen.has(reviewer.login) && seen.add(reviewer.login))
152	    .slice(0, LIST_LIMIT)
153	    .map((reviewer) => ({
154	      login: text(reviewer.login),
155	      state: reviewer.state ?? 'unknown',
156	      reason: reviewer.reason ? text(reviewer.reason) : null,
157	      outdated: Boolean(reviewer.reviewed_head_sha && gate.head_sha && reviewer.reviewed_head_sha !== gate.head_sha)
158	    }))
159	}
160	
161	// The short phrase Entire's web view puts beside each gate, such as "2 of 2 passed".
162	function gateSummary(gate, base) {
163	  const value = gate.value ?? {}
164	  if (gate.state === 'not_run') return 'Not evaluated yet'
165	  if (gate.gate_type === 'approvals') return `${value.approved ?? 0} of ${value.required ?? 0}`
166	  if (gate.gate_type === 'checks') {
167	    const runs = value.checks ?? []
168	    const total = value.total_count ?? runs.length
169	    if (!total) return 'No checks'
170	    return `${runs.filter((run) => run.conclusion === 'success').length} of ${total} passed`
171	  }
172	  if (gate.gate_type === 'findings') {
173	    const blocking = value.agent_blocking_findings ?? gate.finding_count ?? 0
174	    return blocking ? `${blocking} blocking` : 'None blocking'
175	  }
176	  if (gate.gate_type === 'up_to_date' && value.behind_by > 0) return `${value.behind_by} behind ${base ?? 'base'}`
177	  return null
178	}
179	
180	function approvers(gate) {
181	  const reviewers = [gate.reviewers, gate.value?.reviewers].flat().filter(Boolean)
182	  return reviewers.filter((reviewer) => reviewer.state === 'approved' && reviewer.login).map((reviewer) => reviewer.login)
183	}
184	
185	// The findings gate carries the review: which reviewers ran and what they found, by severity.
186	function reviewSummary(gate) {
187	  const value = gate.value ?? {}
188	  const reviewers = (value.reviewers ?? []).map((reviewer) => ({
189	    name: reviewer.name ?? 'Reviewer',
190	    kind: reviewer.kind ?? null,
191	    status: reviewer.status ?? 'unknown',
192	    blocking: reviewer.blocking_findings ?? 0,
193	    nonBlocking: reviewer.non_blocking_findings ?? 0
194	  }))
195	  return {
196	    status: gate.status ?? 'unknown',
197	    verdict: reviewVerdict(value, reviewers),
198	    inFlight: Boolean(value.review_in_flight),
199	    reviewers,
200	    severity: {
201	      high: value.agent_findings?.high ?? 0,
202	      medium: value.agent_findings?.medium ?? 0,
203	      low: value.agent_findings?.low ?? 0
204	    }
205	  }
206	}
207	
208	const SEVERITY_ORDER = { high: 0, medium: 1, low: 2 }
209	
210	// Open findings first, then by severity, as the web view lists them.
211	// A review agent's signal is true, a fail in Entire's web view, when it reports any defect, blocking
212	// or not. The findings gate is a separate question: it fails only on findings at its minimum severity.
213	function reviewVerdict(value, reviewers) {
214	  if (value.review_in_flight) return 'running'
215	  const done = reviewers.filter((reviewer) => reviewer.status === 'completed')
216	  if (!done.length) return 'not_run'
217	  return done.some((reviewer) => reviewer.blocking + reviewer.nonBlocking > 0) ? 'fail' : 'pass'
218	}
219	
220	function findingsSummary({ counts = {}, findings = [] }) {
221	  const ordered = [...findings].sort(
222	    (a, b) => (a.status === 'open' ? 0 : 1) - (b.status === 'open' ? 0 : 1) || (SEVERITY_ORDER[a.severity] ?? 3) - (SEVERITY_ORDER[b.severity] ?? 3)
223	  )
224	  return {
225	    open: counts.Open ?? 0,
226	    high: counts.OpenHigh ?? 0,
227	    medium: counts.OpenMedium ?? 0,
228	    low: counts.OpenLow ?? 0,
229	    resolved: counts.Resolved ?? 0,
230	    dismissed: counts.Dismissed ?? 0,
231	    stale: counts.Stale ?? 0,
232	    items: ordered.slice(0, FINDING_LIMIT).map((finding) => {
233	      const location = finding.location ?? {}
234	      const body = String(finding.body ?? '')
235	      return {
236	        // Agents often leave the title empty and lead the body with the defect.
237	        title: (finding.title || body.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s|\n/)[0] || '').slice(0, TEXT_LIMIT),
238	        body: body.slice(0, BODY_LIMIT * 2),
239	        severity: finding.severity ?? null,
240	        confidence: typeof finding.confidence === 'number' ? finding.confidence : null,
241	        status: finding.status ?? null,
242	        reason: finding.statusReason ? String(finding.statusReason).slice(0, BODY_LIMIT) : null,
243	        stale: finding.staleOutcome === 'stale',
244	        file: location.filePath ?? location.file_path ?? null,
245	        line: location.startLine ?? location.start_line ?? null,
246	        endLine: location.endLine ?? location.end_line ?? null
247	      }
248	    })
249	  }
250	}

1	// Orca forks this module in a Node worker on the desktop host and calls activate once. Orca starts it
2	// for a command, an event, or the panel's first plugin.request, and stops it after 5 idle minutes;
3	// the panel's next request starts it again.
4	import { actionRequest, runAction } from './actions.mjs'
5	import { connectionNotice, connectionReport } from './doctor.mjs'
6	import { createPanelData } from './panel.mjs'
7	import { collectSnapshot } from './snapshot.mjs'
8	
9	// Entire writes its checkpoint data as an agent stops, so let it settle before reading.
10	const AGENT_SETTLE_MS = 3000
11	
12	export default function activate(orca) {
13	  const notify = (notice, signal) =>
14	    orca.host.call('notifications.show', notice, { signal }).catch((error) => {
15	      console.error(`Notification failed: ${error.message}`)
16	    })
17	
18	  // Tells open panels to ask for the data again. A post carries at most 256 KiB, so the data
19	  // itself goes back through the panel's request.
20	  const announce = () => {
21	    try {
22	      orca.panels?.post('entire.changed', {})
23	    } catch (error) {
24	      console.error(`Posting to the panel failed: ${error.message}`)
25	    }
26	  }
27	
28	  // Each snapshot's report also goes to the plugin's Logs, since the command palette drops a
29	  // command's result.
30	  const collect = async (signal) => {
31	    const snapshot = await collectSnapshot(orca, { signal })
32	    console.log(connectionReport(orca, snapshot))
33	    return snapshot
34	  }
35	
36	  // Only a read that found the workspace changed the data; a post after one that didn't would have the
37	  // panel fetch the old data and take it as news.
38	  const announceIfAdded = (snapshot) => {
39	    if (snapshot.workspace) announce()
40	    return snapshot
41	  }
42	
43	  const panel = createPanelData({
44	    collect: () => collect().then(announceIfAdded),
45	    readContext: () => orca.host.call('workspace.readContext', {})
46	  })
47	
48	  orca.panels?.handle('entire.data', async () => panel.data)
49	  orca.panels?.handle('entire.read', async (input) => panel.read({ maxAgeMs: Math.max(0, Number(input?.maxAgeMs) || 0) }))
50	
51	  // Approve or merge the trail the panel showed in the workspace the click was in, then read Entire
52	  // again so the panel shows the result. Only the panel's confirmed click sends this; the worker never
53	  // acts on its own.
54	  orca.panels?.handle('entire.act', async (input) => {
55	    const request = actionRequest(input)
56	    let message
57	    try {
58	      message = await runAction(request, { data: panel.data })
59	    } catch (error) {
60	      console.error(`Trail ${request.action} #${request.trail} on ${request.branch} failed: ${error.message}`)
61	      throw error
62	    }
63	    console.log(message)
64	    // The action happened even if this read fails; the panel's next read catches up.
65	    const data = await panel.readAgain().catch((error) => {
66	      console.error(`Reading Entire after the ${request.action} failed: ${error.message}`)
67	      return panel.data
68	    })
69	    return { message, data }
70	  })
71	
72	  // A command must answer within 30 seconds, so it reads on its own, under its own signal.
73	  async function refresh(signal) {
74	    const snapshot = announceIfAdded(panel.add(await collect(signal)))
75	    return connectionReport(orca, snapshot)
76	  }
77	
78	  orca.commands.register('doctor', async (_args, { signal }) => {
79	    const report = await refresh(signal)
80	    await notify(connectionNotice(report), signal)
81	    return report
82	  })
83	
84	  orca.commands.register('refresh', async (_args, { signal }) => {
85	    const report = await refresh(signal)
86	    const notice = connectionNotice(report)
87	    if (notice.title !== 'Entire: connected') await notify({ ...notice, title: 'Entire: panel updated with a problem' }, signal)
88	    return 'Panel updated'
89	  })
90	
91	  // An agent finishing is when Entire has new checkpoints and sessions to show. Several finishing
92	  // together make one read.
93	  let timer = null
94	  orca.events.on('agent.status.changed', (event) => {
95	    if ((event.mainAgent?.state ?? event.state) !== 'done') return
96	    clearTimeout(timer)
97	    timer = setTimeout(() => {
98	      timer = null
99	      panel.readAgain().catch((error) => console.error(`Refresh failed: ${error.message}`))
100	    }, AGENT_SETTLE_MS)
101	  })
102	}

1	// The panel's two writes to Entire: approve a trail, and merge its change. Each runs only on a click
2	// the panel confirmed, and only on the workspace that click was in: the panel names it by its path
3	// (and paired server), the worker finds its own entry for it, checks the trail there, and runs Entire
4	// for that entry. Focus is not read again, so switching workspaces after the click can't redirect it.
5	import { failureLine, runEntire } from './entire-cli.mjs'
6	import { branchName, serverHost, workspaceHost } from './hosts.mjs'
7	
8	const ACTIONS = {
9	  approve: { verb: 'approve', done: 'Approved' },
10	  merge: { verb: 'merge', done: 'Merged' }
11	}
12	
13	// Entire merges on its server, which checks the gates first; give it longer than a read.
14	const ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000
15	
16	// The panel's input, checked: { action, trail, branch, path, environment }. Throws on anything else.
17	export function actionRequest(input) {
18	  const action = Object.hasOwn(ACTIONS, input?.action) ? input.action : null
19	  if (!action) throw new Error('Unknown trail action')
20	  const trail = Number(input.trail)
21	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(trail) || trail < 1) throw new Error('No trail number to act on')
22	  const branch = branchName(input.branch)
23	  if (!branch) throw new Error('No valid branch to act on')
24	  if (typeof input.path !== 'string' || !input.path) throw new Error('No workspace to act in')
25	  const environment = input.environment ?? null
26	  if (environment !== null && typeof environment !== 'string') throw new Error('No valid paired server to act on')
27	  return { action, trail, branch, path: input.path, environment }
28	}
29	
30	// The worker's entry for the workspace the click was in, or null.
31	export function confirmedEntry(data, { path, environment }) {
32	  return (data?.workspaces ?? []).find((entry) => entry.workspace.path === path && (entry.workspace.server?.environment ?? null) === environment) ?? null
33	}
34	
35	// That workspace must still show the trail the click was for, and for a merge, nothing may block it.
36	export function checkShown(request, entry) {
37	  const value = entry?.data?.trail
38	  const { action, trail, branch } = request
39	  if (!value || value.number !== trail || value.branch !== branch) {
40	    throw new Error(`That workspace no longer shows trail #${trail} on ${branch}, so nothing was done. Check the panel and try again.`)
41	  }
42	  if (!value.open) throw new Error(`Trail #${trail}'s change on ${branch} isn't open, so there is nothing to ${ACTIONS[action].verb}.`)
43	  if (action === 'merge' && (!Array.isArray(value.blockers) || value.blockers.length)) {
44	    throw new Error(`Trail #${trail} can't merge yet: ${(value.blockers ?? ['refresh the panel first']).join('; ')}.`)
45	  }
46	}
47	
48	// Where Entire runs for an entry: its checkout, or for a paired server's workspace, this desktop by
49	// repository. Both act on Entire's server, so a server workspace needs no SSH here.
50	export function entryHost(entry) {
51	  const { path, server } = entry.workspace
52	  if (!server) return workspaceHost(path)
53	  const host = serverHost({ environment: server.environment, path, repoUrl: server.repoUrl, branch: server.branch })
54	  if (!host.repo) throw new Error(`The panel doesn't know ${path} on ${server.environment}'s repository yet. Use ↻ and try again.`)
55	  return host
56	}
57	
58	// --branch picks the change within the trail; a paired server's workspace also names the repository.
59	export function actionArgs({ action, trail, branch }, host) {
60	  const args = ['trail', action, String(trail), '--branch', branch]
61	  return host.kind === 'server' ? [...args, '--repo', host.repo] : args
62	}
63	
64	// Runs the action for the confirmed workspace and answers with a line to show.
65	export async function runAction(request, { data, signal, run = runEntire } = {}) {
66	  const entry = confirmedEntry(data, request)
67	  checkShown(request, entry)
68	  const host = entryHost(entry)
69	  const result = await run(host, actionArgs(request, host), { signal, timeoutMs: ACTION_TIMEOUT_MS })
70	  if (result.code !== 0) throw new Error(`Entire refused to ${ACTIONS[request.action].verb} trail #${request.trail}: ${failureLine(result)}`)
71	  return `${ACTIONS[request.action].done} trail #${request.trail} on ${request.branch}.`
72	}

1	// What the panel shows: the newest snapshot of each workspace the worker read, kept in the worker's
2	// memory. The panel asks for it with plugin.request (the handlers are in main.mjs) and gets all of
3	// it, then picks the focused workspace's entry itself (findEntry in panel/index.html).
4	import { reportLines } from './doctor.mjs'
5	
6	const MAX_WORKSPACES = 10
7	// Orca refuses a plugin.request answer over 1 MiB; leave room for its envelope.
8	const MAX_ANSWER_CHARS = 900_000
9	
10	export function panelEntry(snapshot) {
11	  return { ...snapshot, report: reportLines(snapshot) }
12	}
13	
14	// Same Orca id, same path on the same host, or a terminal they share.
15	function sameWorkspace(entry, other) {
16	  const environment = (e) => e.workspace.server?.environment ?? null
17	  return (
18	    (entry.workspace.id && other.workspace.id === entry.workspace.id) ||
19	    (entry.workspace.path && other.workspace.path === entry.workspace.path && environment(other) === environment(entry)) ||
20	    other.workspace.terminals.some((id) => entry.workspace.terminals.includes(id)) ||
21	    (!other.workspace.path && other.workspace.name === entry.workspace.name && other.workspace.branch === entry.workspace.branch)
22	  )
23	}
24	
25	// A newer entry replaces any for the same workspace, and the oldest go once the answer gets too big.
26	export function mergeEntry(data, entry, { maxChars = MAX_ANSWER_CHARS } = {}) {
27	  const others = (data?.workspaces ?? []).filter((other) => !sameWorkspace(entry, other))
28	  const workspaces = [entry, ...others].slice(0, MAX_WORKSPACES)
29	  while (workspaces.length > 1 && JSON.stringify(workspaces).length > maxChars) workspaces.pop()
30	  return { version: 1, workspaces }
31	}
32	
33	// The entry the panel shows for a readContext result. Keep this the same as findEntry in
34	// panel/index.html: the worker uses it to tell whether the panel's entry is fresh enough.
35	export function findShown(data, context) {
36	  // Orca's workspaceId names the workspace exactly, but a workspace keeps it across a branch checkout,
37	  // so the branch has to match as well. An entry with another known id is another workspace. Panels
38	  // get the id only in its `identity:` form, so without one only entries of that form are ruled out.
39	  const list = (data?.workspaces ?? []).filter((entry) =>
40	    context.workspaceId
41	      ? !entry.workspace.id || entry.workspace.id === context.workspaceId
42	      : !String(entry.workspace.id ?? '').startsWith('identity:')
43	  )
44	  const byId = context.workspaceId && list.find((entry) => entry.workspace.id === context.workspaceId && entry.workspace.branch === context.branch)
45	  if (byId) return byId
46	  const ids = context.terminals.map((terminal) => terminal.id)
47	  // A workspace keeps its terminals when it switches branch, so the branch has to match as well.
48	  const byTerminal = list.find((entry) => entry.workspace.branch === context.branch && entry.workspace.terminals.some((id) => ids.includes(id)))
49	  if (byTerminal) return byTerminal
50	  // Many repos share a name and branch such as main/main: only when terminals can't tell them apart
51	  // and exactly one entry matches.
52	  const byName = list.filter(
53	    (entry) =>
54	      !(ids.length > 0 && entry.workspace.terminals.length > 0) && entry.workspace.name === context.displayName && entry.workspace.branch === context.branch
55	  )
56	  return byName.length === 1 ? byName[0] : null
57	}
58	
59	// The panel's data and the reads that fill it. `collect` reads Entire for the focused workspace (a
60	// snapshot), `readContext` asks Orca which workspace that is. One read runs at a time: a request
61	// that finds one running waits for it, and reads again only if focus moved meanwhile.
62	export function createPanelData({ collect, readContext, now = Date.now }) {
63	  let data = null
64	  let reading = null
65	
66	  function add(snapshot) {
67	    if (snapshot.workspace) data = mergeEntry(data, panelEntry(snapshot))
68	    return snapshot
69	  }
70	
71	  // A read outlives the request that started it, since others may be waiting on it, so it takes no
72	  // signal; Entire's own timeouts bound it.
73	  function readNow() {
74	    reading ??= collect().then(add).finally(() => {
75	      reading = null
76	    })
77	    return reading
78	  }
79	
80	  // A read that couldn't find the focused workspace (its lookup failed) added nothing, so answering
81	  // with the data would pass the old data off as this read's. Fail instead: the panel shows why and
82	  // retries on its schedule.
83	  async function readFresh() {
84	    const snapshot = await readNow()
85	    if (!snapshot.workspace) throw new Error(snapshot.problem ?? 'Entire was read for no workspace')
86	    return data
87	  }
88	
89	  async function shown() {
90	    const context = await readContext()
91	    return context ? findShown(data, context) : null
92	  }
93	
94	  return {
95	    get data() {
96	      return data
97	    },
98	    add,
99	    // Reads Entire unless the panel's entry for the focused workspace is younger than maxAgeMs (0
100	    // always reads), and answers with all the data.
101	    async read({ maxAgeMs = 0 } = {}) {
102	      if (maxAgeMs > 0) {
103	        const at = Date.parse((await shown())?.at)
104	        if (Number.isFinite(at) && now() - at < maxAgeMs) return data
105	      }
106	      if (reading) {
107	        const joined = await reading.catch(() => null)
108	        if (joined && (await shown())?.at === joined.at) return data
109	      }
110	      return readFresh()
111	    },
112	    // Reads Entire with a read that starts now: one already running may have begun before what the
113	    // caller wants to see, such as an agent's last checkpoint, so it waits for that one and reads again.
114	    async readAgain() {
115	      if (reading) await reading.catch(() => null)
116	      return readFresh()
117	    }
118	  }
119	}

1	# Entire for Orca: plan
2	
3	Bring Entire (trails, findings, approvals, checkpoints) into Orca's UI as an Orca plugin, the way
4	Orca already surfaces GitHub pull requests and checks.
5	
6	Status: phases 0 and 0.5 done. 0.1.0 is listed in Orca's community catalog (2026-11-14), as
7	`petercr.entire`. Next: screenshots of the real panel for 0.1.1, then phase 1's spikes and phase 2's
8	commands.
9	
10	## Environment
11	
12	- Orca desktop runs on Windows (1.4.250 since 2026-11-05; the plan began on 1.4.245). Plugins are in
13	  alpha: manifest format 2. The plugin targets Orca 1.4.246 or later for host API 1.2.
14	- Most Orca and Entire projects live in WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...`). Others live
15	  on a VPS that Orca reaches as a paired Orca server (`orca environment list`: "Endo VPS Server", an
16	  orcad over an SSH tunnel to `ubuntu@15.204.88.195`).
17	- Entire CLI `0.12.3-nightly` on both sides: WSL (keyring login) and Windows in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`
18	  (Credential Manager login).
19	- This repo: `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`, origin
20	  `entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/et/entire-repos/orca-entire-extension`, Entire enabled.
21	
22	## What Orca's plugin API allows (1.4.245, updated for 1.4.250)
23	
24	Sources: `docs/reference/plugin-*.md` and `src/shared/plugins/**` in github.com/stablyai/orca.
25	
26	- `execution: "trusted-worker"`: `main` runs in a Node process Orca forks on the desktop host (Windows
27	  here). It has full Node access, but its env is an allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, TEMP and a few
28	  Windows system variables; no APPDATA). Idle workers stop after 5 minutes with nothing in flight, and a
29	  command must answer within 30 seconds.
30	- Host API 1.0: `workspace.readContext` returns `{ branch, displayName, terminals: [{ id }] }` with no
31	  path; `notifications.show`; `terminal.sendText` (worker only); `storage.*`, `secrets.*` and
32	  `settings.*` (worker only).
33	- Events (at most 3): `workspace.created`, `workspace.removed`, `agent.status.changed`.
34	- The command palette ignores a command's return value. The Run button in Settings → Plugins shows its
35	  first 200 characters in a toast. Worker stdout and stderr go to the plugin's Logs (last 200 lines).
36	- Panels are sealed: no network, no browser permissions (so no async Clipboard API;
37	  `execCommand('copy')` in a click works), links only through `orca.shell.openExternal` (1.1).
38	- Host API 1.2 (Orca 1.4.246) added the panel channel: a panel calls `orca.plugin.request(name,
39	  input, { timeoutMs })`, which starts the worker if needed and runs the handler it registered with
40	  `orca.panels.handle`; the worker posts with `orca.panels.post` (fire and forget, 256 KiB) and the
41	  panel listens with `orca.plugin.on`. Answers go up to 1 MiB, requests up to 120 s. A panel also
42	  hears `workspace.changed` and agent events with `orca.on`. 1.2 also brought `agents.list`; 1.3
43	  brings `workspace.list` (every workspace with its path and host, worker only), which could replace
44	  much of `src/worker/workspace.mjs` once the installed Orca offers it.
45	- Before 1.2 the panel worked only from a development folder: the worker wrote its data into the
46	  panel file (installed copies are hash-checked), and ↻ reached the worker through Orca's audit log.
47	  Both stopgaps are gone (branch `panel-channel`).
48	- Reserved but not shipped: `taskSources`, `statusBarItems`, `sidebarCards`, `connections`, `settings`,
49	  `hooks`, `skills`, `mcpServers`.
50	- 1.4.250 has the `orca plugin` CLI: `validate`, `inspect` (content hash), `release-entry`, `logs`,
51	  and `dev request` to call a panel handler. Load the plugin through Settings → Plugins →
52	  Development folders.
53	- `publisher` is deprecated: Orca names the publisher after the repository owner for catalog and Git
54	  installs (`petercr.entire`) and `local` for a folder (`local.entire`). Leaving it out needs
55	  `>=1.4.246`. Ids may not start with `orca-`.
56	
57	## Spike results (2026-10-30)
58	
59	Run from Windows Node with the worker's env allowlist:
60	
61	- `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire trail list ... --json` works with the WSL
62	  login, in 0.6–0.8 s per call.
63	- Orca's CLI (`resources\bin\orca.exe` beside the app) works once APPDATA is derived from USERPROFILE.
64	  `worktree list` takes about 2.1 s.
65	- `readContext` terminal ids are Orca CLI terminal handles. `orca terminal show --terminal <id> --json`
66	  returns the workspace's `worktreePath` (e.g. `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\peterc\ccw`), which gives the
67	  distro and Linux path.
68	- Entire has `--json` on `status`, `trail list/show/approvals/finding`, and `trail watch --json`
69	  (the trail's SSE stream as JSON lines). `trail show` exits 1 when the branch has no trail.
70	
71	## Architecture
72	
73	- One `trusted-worker` plugin. The worker is the only part that talks to Entire.
74	- Find the focused workspace's path: first terminal handle from `readContext` → `orca terminal show`.
75	  Fallback: match branch and name against `orca worktree list`. This is a stopgap until `readContext`
76	  carries a path (see the asks below).
77	- Run Entire where the repo and its login live. For a WSL path, use
78	  `wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd <path> -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire ...`. For a local path, run
79	  `entire` directly. For a paired server's workspace (a VPS), run this desktop's `entire` outside any
80	  checkout with `--repo <origin URL> --branch <branch>`: trails and findings live on Entire's server, so
81	  they read fine. Status, checkpoints and the diff need the checkout: the worker runs them over SSH to
82	  the server's Orca SSH target, with the key in the Windows ssh-agent. Without that, the panel says why.
83	- Shell out to the Entire CLI rather than calling its REST API. The CLI owns login, contexts and cell
84	  routing, so the plugin never holds a token. `entire api` covers gaps.
85	- Refresh the focused workspace on `agent.status.changed`, when focus moves to it or its branch
86	  changes (`workspace.changed`, plus a 5-second `readContext` poll for branch checkouts) and every
87	  5 minutes. The panel asks, the worker reads Entire only when its data for the workspace is older
88	  than the request allows, and the panel shows "Checking…" while a read runs. Later, tail
89	  `trail watch --json` while the worker is alive.
90	- Panels only render what the worker hands them: its in-memory snapshots (up to 10 workspaces,
91	  matched to the focused one by terminal id, then name and branch), through `entire.read` and
92	  `entire.data`. Feature-detect with `orca.host.has(...)` so a too-old Orca gets a clear message.
93	- Entire text (intent, findings, comments) is untrusted: render it as text and never execute it.
94	
95	## GitHub feature → Entire equivalent
96	
97	| Orca + GitHub today             | Entire equivalent                                  | Unblocked by                     |
98	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
99	| PR and CI notifications         | trail events → notifications                       | shipped API                      |
100	| Create, approve, merge a PR     | `trail create`, `approve`, `merge` as commands     | shipped API                      |
101	| Checks sidebar, review comments | trail panel: gates, CI runs, findings, approvals   | Orca #25256                      |
102	| Issues on Tasks → new workspace | trails tab → start a workspace on the change       | Orca #26282                      |
103	| PR badge on the workspace card  | trail badge on the card                            | #26282, then a forge provider    |
104	
105	For `et/` repos (`entire://` remotes, like this one) Orca has no forge integration at all, so this
106	plugin is the only one. For GitHub repos it sits beside Orca's GitHub support.
107	
108	## Phases
109	
110	- [x] 0. Repo on Windows, Entire enabled in WSL and on Windows, project added to Orca.
111	- [x] 0.5 Smoke test: load the dev plugin and run **Entire: Check connection** in a WSL workspace and in
112	      this one. Both reported connected in a Windows notification.
113	- [ ] 1. Spikes: real trail JSON fixtures (create a test trail), `trail watch` through `wsl.exe` versus
114	      the 5-minute reaper, the plugin consent flow, latency budget.
115	- [ ] 2. v0.1 on shipped Orca: commands (show trail, findings, approve, merge, create, refresh) and
116	      notifications when an agent finishes and on trail events. Approve and merge are panel buttons
117	      (handler `entire.act`, two clicks each). Merge is enabled only when `mergeBlockers` finds the
118	      change approved, with no failing or pending blocking gate and no conflicts. It never passes
119	      `--force`, and Entire checks the gates again on its side.
120	- [ ] 3. Trail panel. A stopgap panel (repo status, the trail and its merge gates, recent
121	      checkpoints, connection check, a ↻ that works while the worker runs) works from a development
122	      folder. Trail #1 links `plugin-scaffold`; its JSON is `test/fixtures/trail-show.json`, and a
123	      reviewed, merged change is `test/fixtures/trail-367-*.json`. The Trail section follows Entire's
124	      web view (change, code review, merge gates, findings) from `trail show` and `trail finding list`,
125	      plus `git diff --shortstat` for the line counts. Not shown: the web view's Confidence, Risk,
126	      Drift and Security scores, which no CLI command or API type exposes. Since host API 1.2 the
127	      panel asks its worker for the data, so it works installed too.
128	- [ ] 4. Trails tab on the Tasks page and a settings form (Orca #26282).
129	- [ ] 5. Deeper: status bar item, forge provider for `entire://` remotes, Entire agent hooks and skills,
130	      checkpoints, `entire why`, `entire review`.
131	- [x] 6. Distribution through Orca's community catalog (researched 2026-11-05). Community plugins
132	      are listed by machine, not reviewed: a public GitHub repo with `orca-plugin.json` at its root,
133	      the `orca-plugin` topic and a `vX.Y.Z` tag. Within about an hour the plugin shows at
134	      `onorca.dev/plugins/petercr/orca-entire-extension` and in `stablyai/orca-community-plugins`,
135	      pinned to the tag's commit and content hash. A listed version never changes, and a moved tag
136	      is refused. The official catalog (`stablyai/orca-plugins`) takes only Stably's own plugins.
137	      Exclusions: the validator fails, no license GitHub detects, binaries or symlinks, a publisher
138	      other than the repo owner, a fork, an archived repo, the listing policy (no paywall, no
139	      impersonation, no tracking, no obfuscated code). The Entire team has approved the name.
140	      Users get updates on their own unless one asks for more access (a capability, command, panel
141	      or event), which Orca makes them approve again.
142	  - [x] The panel asks its worker for data over host API 1.2 instead of reading a file the worker
143	        rewrites (branch `panel-channel`).
144	  - [x] Manifest: `engines.orca` `>=1.4.246`, no `publisher`, `license` MIT, `repository`; a
145	        `LICENSE` file.
146	  - [x] Try the channel in Orca: approve `local.entire`, switch workspaces, ↻, let an agent finish,
147	        and leave Orca idle past 5 minutes so the worker stops and the panel's next request restarts it
148	        (works, 2026-11-05).
149	  - [x] A README for users: what they need (Entire CLI installed and logged in where the repos live,
150	        Orca restarted after installing it), what the plugin runs (`entire`, `git`, `ssh`, `wsl.exe`),
151	        that it opts out of Entire's telemetry, what it reads of Orca's own files (the SSH targets in
152	        `profile-state.db`), and an install link,
153	        `https://onorca.dev/plugins/petercr.entire?catalog=community` (branch `user-readme`).
154	  - [x] Say which platforms work: the README's table marks Windows, WSL and paired servers as tested,
155	        and macOS and Linux as untested. `orcaCliPath` expects Orca's CLI where Windows has it, and
156	        reading SSH targets is Windows-only. Trying macOS or Linux is still open.
157	  - [ ] Optional listing images: a cover (16:10, at least 800×500, at most 1024 KB) and up to six
158	        screenshots (at least 1280×800, at most 1536 KB) that show the real panel. The cover is
159	        `images/cover.jpg` (1506×941, no Entire logo); the README opens with `images/banner.jpg`,
160	        which carries Entire's logo and says Unofficial. Screenshots are still to do. GitHub's
161	        social preview has no API: upload it under the repo's Settings → General → Social preview.
162	  - [x] Release: bump `version` (0.1.0), `orca plugin validate .`, commit, `git tag -a v0.1.0 -m
163	        v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`, `gh repo edit petercr/orca-entire-extension --add-topic
164	        orca-plugin`, then check the listing page. Tagged on `f18c7f8` and listed on 2026-11-14:
165	        `onorca.dev/plugins/petercr/orca-entire-extension`, state `listed` in
166	        `stablyai/orca-community-plugins`. Later releases: bump `version`, tag `vX.Y.Z` on `main`;
167	        a listed version never changes, so every change needs a new tag.
168	
169	## Asks for the Orca team
170	
171	1. ~~A channel from a panel to its own worker~~: shipped in host API 1.2 (Orca 1.4.246).
172	2. `workspace.readContext`: add the worktree id, path and host (local, WSL, SSH, paired server). For a
173	   paired server's workspace it now gives only the repo's name, with no branch or terminals.
174	3. Task sources and plugin settings (#26282), with a start recipe that can check out an existing branch.
175	4. Status bar items and sidebar cards (#23143, #26951).
176	5. Opening external URLs from panels and workers (#27568).
177	6. Long-lived worker subscriptions: the 5-minute idle reaper stops `trail watch`.
178	7. A way to run a command on the workspace's host (WSL, SSH, paired server) from a worker, without a
179	   terminal tab.
180	
181	## Risks and open questions
182	
183	- Phases 4–5 depend on Orca work: #26282 active (task sources; plugin settings shipped in 1.4.246),
184	  #15315 (forge providers) stale since August. Phase 3's channel shipped in host API 1.2.
185	- A paired server's workspace reaches `readContext` as its repo's display name, an empty branch and
186	  no terminals (seen 2026-11-01): the desktop runtime doesn't hold it. The worker matches the repo name
187	  against each paired server's `orca repo list` and `worktree list --environment`. Two worktrees of one
188	  repo on a server can't be told apart, and the panel says so. The Orca CLI runs commands there only in
189	  visible terminal tabs, so the worker uses its own SSH (2026-11-01): it needs the key in the Windows
190	  ssh-agent, and it finds the address in Orca's private profile database (`sshTargets`), whose shape
191	  Orca can change without notice. Ask #7 would remove both.
192	- Both sides run Entire 0.12.3-nightly. On Windows, `entire status` reports this repo's 7 Codex hooks
193	  as needing trust approval in Codex (`/hooks`); that only matters when using Codex here.
194	  `entire agent add codex` and `entire doctor` rewrite committed hook files, so run them on a branch.
195	- A worker's PATH comes from Orca's environment at launch. Restart Orca after installing Entire on
196	  Windows.
197	- Can #26282's start recipe check out an existing branch, or only branch off a base?

18	    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => stdout.push(chunk))

# Entire for Orca

![An orca in an Entire T-shirt splashes beside the words Entire for Orca ADE: bring the power of Entire into Orca ADE, with trails, findings and checkpoints. Marked unofficial.](images/banner.jpg)

An [Orca](https://onorca.dev) plugin that shows [Entire](https://entire.com) trails, findings and checkpoints
for the workspace you're working in, in a panel beside your terminals. It gives Entire the place in Orca
that GitHub pull requests and checks already have.

It's a community plugin. It only reads, except for the panel's **Approve** and **Merge** buttons,
which write to Entire only when you click and then confirm. It never creates or changes anything else.

## What you get

**The Entire panel** (the layers icon in the right sidebar) follows the focused workspace and shows:

- the repo's Entire status and any active agent sessions
- the branch's trail: its change, the code review, the merge gates (approvals, checks, findings, up to
  date) and the findings, each of which you can copy, one at a time or all together
- **Approve** and **Merge** buttons for the trail's change. Each asks you to click again to confirm.
  Merge stays greyed out until the change is approved (when the repo needs approvals), no blocking
  gate is failing or pending, and there are no conflicts; the line under it says what it's waiting on.
  Entire checks the gates again before it merges, and the plugin never forces a merge.
- the branch's recent checkpoints
- a connection check that says what worked and what didn't

It reads Entire when you switch workspaces or branches, when an agent finishes, and every 5 minutes.
↻ reads it now. **Report a problem on GitHub**, at the bottom of the panel, opens a new issue here with
the versions filled in.

**Commands** in the command palette:

- **Entire: Check connection** runs the same check and reports it as a notification.
- **Entire: Refresh panel** reads Entire for the focused workspace now.

## Requirements

- **Orca 1.4.246 or later.**
- **The Entire CLI, installed and logged in where your repos live:**
  - Repos on this computer: Entire on the PATH Orca starts with.
  - Repos in WSL: Entire inside that WSL distro, logged in there. The plugin runs it through `wsl.exe`
    in a login shell, so `~/.local/bin` counts.
  - Repos on a paired Orca server: Entire on this computer, logged in to an account that can see the
    repository, for the trail and findings. For status and checkpoints, the plugin also needs SSH to the
    server (see [Paired servers](#paired-servers)).
- **Entire enabled in the repo** (`entire enable`) for its status and checkpoints. A repo without it
  still shows its trail.
- **Restart Orca after installing Entire**, so the plugin sees it on PATH.

## Install

Turn on plugins in **Settings → Plugins** if they're off. Then open the plugin in Orca's community
catalog, <https://onorca.dev/plugins/petercr.entire?catalog=community>, and install it. Orca shows
what the plugin asks for before you approve it:

- **Workspace (read):** which workspace is focused, its branch and its terminals, to know which repo to
  read.
- **Notifications:** for **Entire: Check connection** and for problems found by **Entire: Refresh
  panel**.
- **Agents (read):** to read Entire again when an agent finishes.

Then open the **Entire** panel.

## Platforms

| Where the workspace is | Status                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows                | Tested                                                                       |
| WSL, from Windows      | Tested                                                                       |
| A paired Orca server   | Tested from Windows. Status and checkpoints over SSH work on Windows only.   |
| macOS, Linux           | Not tested. Finding the workspace expects Orca's CLI where Windows has it, so it may fail; reports welcome. |

## Paired servers

Orca tells plugins only the repo name of a workspace on a paired server, with no branch or path. The
plugin finds it in the server's worktree list, then:

- reads the trail and findings with this computer's Entire, by the repo's origin URL and branch;
- reads status, checkpoints and the diff size over SSH to the server, using the address Orca saved
  for it. SSH runs with `BatchMode`, so it can't ask for a passphrase: add the key to the ssh-agent
  (`ssh-add`) first.

The plugin now handles a repo with several trails or pull requests open, on the `trail-actions` branch, uncommitted.

**What was wrong.** The worker only ran `entire trail show` for the checked-out branch, so a second open change in the same repo was invisible, and Approve and Merge could only act on that one trail.

**Worker.** A new module, [trails.mjs](C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension\src\worker\trails.mjs), finds the repo's other open changes:

- It parses the origin URL into Entire's project reference (GitHub or `entire://` remotes), since `trail list` needs `--project` and the listing carries no changes.
- It lists the repo's open trails, shows the newest 10 (four at a time), and keeps each change that is open in this repo, except the focused branch's. A trail stays "open" on Entire after its change merges, so only the shows tell which changes are live.
- Each kept change gets its findings and, on local and WSL checkouts, its line counts against the base. SSH checkouts skip the counts to avoid a round trip per trail.
- The snapshot now carries `data.trails`, the focused branch's trail first with `here: true`, and a new "Other trails" row in the Connection check.
- The action check in [actions.mjs](C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension\src\worker\actions.mjs) finds the clicked trail anywhere in that list, so Approve and Merge work on any listed change whatever branch is checked out.

**Panel.** When the repo has more than the focused branch's trail, a picker appears above the trail detail: one row per open change with its number, title, branch, a "this branch" marker, and its Ready, Blocked, Open or Merged state. Clicking a row shows that trail's change, review, gates, findings and buttons. The pick is remembered per workspace and falls back to the focused branch's trail if the worker stops listing it. When the focused branch has no trail but others exist, the panel says so and lists them.

**Verified.** All 86 unit tests pass, including new ones for URL parsing, change selection, the fake-Entire read, the action check and the panel's picking. The Orca harness run against the WSL `one_test` workspace read trail 517 and checked the newest 10 of 50+ open trails in 3.5 seconds. That run also caught a real bug: excluding the focused change by branch name alone double-listed it, so it now also excludes the change Entire marks current.

**Caveats.** The trails step adds a few seconds per read, which could push a slow WSL read past the 30-second limit on the two palette commands. Panel reads have 100 seconds and are unaffected. I have not seen the picker rendered in Orca itself. To try it, toggle the plugin off and on and focus a repo with several open changes.

## What

A repo with several trails or pull requests open showed only the checked-out branch's trail. Now the panel lists every open change of the repository and lets you pick one to see and act on.

**Worker**
- New `src/worker/trails.mjs`: lists the repo's open trails with `trail list --project` (the project parsed from the origin URL, GitHub or `entire://`), shows the newest 10 four at a time, and keeps each change that is open in this repo, except the focused branch's, which the snapshot already shows. Each gets its findings and, on local and WSL checkouts, its line counts against the base. A trail stays `open` on Entire after its change merges, so only the shows tell which changes are live.
- The snapshot carries `data.trails` (the focused branch's first, `here: true`) and a new "Other trails" row in the Connection check.
- The action check finds the clicked trail anywhere in that list, so Approve and Merge work on any listed change whatever branch is checked out.

**Panel**
- When the repo has more than the focused branch's trail, a picker above the detail shows one row per open change: number, title, branch, a "this branch" marker and its merge state. Clicking a row shows that change's review, gates, findings and buttons. The pick is remembered per workspace and falls back to the focused branch's trail.

**Keeping reads under Orca's 30 s command limit**
- The trails read runs alongside the branch's own steps rather than after them, reusing the focused branch's `trail show`.
- It runs under a deadline: 20 s for a palette command, 60 s for a panel request. Past it no new call starts, calls in flight get only the time left plus a short grace, and the Connection check row says how many trails or findings were skipped. Whatever was read in time still shows.

### Medium finding

**Location:** `src/worker/trails.mjs:116`

If an off-branch diff starts shortly before the 20-second command deadline (`src/worker/main.mjs:13`), this check enters `diffStat`, whose four possible git attempts each retain a separate 15-second timeout (`src/worker/git.mjs:24-28`, `src/worker/process.mjs:5`). A large diff or slow WSL invocation can therefore keep the snapshot waiting beyond Orca’s 30-second command limit, even when the focused branch’s steps finished successfully. Propagate the remaining budget into git calls and stop fallback attempts when it expires.

### Low finding

**Location:** `src/worker/trails.mjs:112`

For the repository's other open changes, `base` comes straight from Entire's findings (`findings.value?.trail?.base`) and goes to `diff(checkout, base, …)` without the `safeRef` check that `snapshot.mjs` uses for the focused branch. `diffStat`'s second attempt passes `${base}...${to}` as a bare argument, so a trail base such as `--output=<path>` makes `git diff` treat it as an option and create or truncate a file on the user's machine, at a path that ends in `...<branch>`. Wrap the base in `safeRef` here, or validate it inside `diffStat`.

### Low finding

**Location:** `src/worker/trails.mjs:77`

When `repoRef` can't parse the origin URL, the step text includes the first 80 characters of the raw URL. Credential-bearing URLs (`REDACTED`, or `REDACTED`) fail the regex, because the userinfo has a colon or the host isn't GitHub, so the token ends up in the panel, in the plugin Logs through `connectionReport`, and in the "Check connection" notification. Strip the userinfo (or leave the URL out) before putting it in the message.
Three fixes: bound the git calls by the remaining budget, validate the base with `safeRef`, and keep credentials out of the step text. Let me see the diff helper first.
